Transfer applicants have a separate route requiring a 3.7 college GPA and, for fewer than 30 college credits, qualifying test scores.

supports: identity: National English Honor Society (NEHS) confirms NEHS Scholarships.

value: Over $90,000 in the scholarship fund, with 30 or more recipients in an average year; individual amounts depend on submission quality and volume. At least one $5,000 Dr. William C. Johnson scholarship is awarded each year.

application: Through AwardSpring, submit a critical analytical essay of at most 850 words including quotations/references, double-spaced in 12-point font with MLA documentation, as an anonymous PDF labeled for the prompt. eligibility: Current high-school seniors who are NEHS student members at an active chapter and plan to attend an accredited two-year college or four-year university, anywhere in the world. Any major is allowed.

supports: identity: Civil Air Patrol confirms CAP Cadet Academic Scholarships (CadetInvest).

value: Academic awards generally range from $1,000 to $2,500 for tuition, books, or room and board at a postsecondary school. The Board of Governors award provides $2,500 each to two cadets; other amounts vary.
deadline: Applications are projected to open December 15, 2026 at noon Central and close January 15, 2027 at noon Central, including unit and wing approval.

application: In e-Services Registration Zone, submit the primary Scholarship application and at least one academic scholarship subevent, a resume of no more than two pages and one to three recommendations about your CAP accomplishments. Combine multiple documents of the same type; unit and wing leadership must approve before the deadline. Some awards require extra documents or an essay.

eligibility: Current active CAP cadets in good standing, with the Billy Mitchell Award or higher, who are high school seniors, graduates or GED holders and have applied to or been accepted by a postsecondary school. Enroll during the award year and maintain acceptable academic and discipline standards. No scholarship recipient from the preceding three years is eligible. Individual awards add requirements: Etheridge requires a B average; Schroder requires a STEM major and original essay; August Trust is for Arizona Wing STEM or aviation cadets; Diaz is restricted to listed Florida squadrons; Mullins is need-based for Michigan Wing cadets.

value: National Winner $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Merit Awards $100 (separately for brass and voice)
deadline: Registration opens November 1, 2026 on Acceptd; video deadline December 2, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. ET

application: Register on Acceptd from November 1, 2026 and upload unedited, fixed-camera performance videos by December 2 at 3 PM Eastern. Seven finalists per category perform live in St. Louis; the senior rehearsal, competition and winners’ concert are April 2, 3 and 4, 2027.

eligibility: Brass players (trumpet, horn, euphonium, trombone or tuba) and singers ages 15 to 18 on January 1, 2027, studying with a teacher. Previous national first-place winners cannot reenter the same level and category.

supports: identity: AATSP Exams (National Spanish Examinations) confirms NSE/NPE Senior Scholarship (Traditional Scholarship).

application: Ask your teacher to select you, then use the linked Google Form and media release. Follow the required filenames.

eligibility: Graduating seniors who scored at or above the 75th percentile on NSE/NPE in both 2024-25 and 2025-26 and take the exam in 2026-27. Applicants may also apply for SHH awards but may receive only one scholarship.

application: College determines eligibility using official final high-school transcript, residency/citizenship verification and any applicable test/rank documentation. deadline: No separate statewide scholarship application. Submit required admission, official academic records and eligibility documents by the college financial-aid office's deadlines; mid-year graduates require additional early-graduation documents.
identity: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education confirms LIFE Scholarship.

value: Up to $5,000 annually at eligible four-year institutions ($4,700 tuition plus $300 book allowance); two-year amounts based on eligible tuition/book costs, capped at $5,000. Cost-of-attendance ceiling applies with other gift aid. Normally two terms for one-year certificates, four for associates, six for approved 68-credit associates, eight for first bachelors, ten for approved five-year degrees. Renewal requires 3.0 LIFE GPA and average 30 earned credits per academic year. Approved STEM, accounting or education majors may add up to $2,500 annually starting sophomore year; education recipients sign a South Carolina public-school teaching obligation.

eligibility: South Carolina resident and U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident at high-school graduation and enrolment; full-time eligible degree student. Four-year freshman route requires two of three: 3.0 unrounded SC Uniform Grading Policy GPA, SAT 1100 or ACT equivalent 22, top 30% approved UGP class rank. Nonranking schools require GPA plus test route. Two-year freshman route requires 3.0 UGP GPA. Eligible SC schools/homeschool or qualified out-of-state dependent route applies; later college eligibility can be earned with LIFE GPA/credit requirements. Enhancement requires approved major and normally 14 eligible math/science/accounting credits by end of first college year; education route has separate service-contract requirements.

supports: identity: West Virginia Higher Education Policy Commission confirms PROMISE Scholarship.

value: Up to $5,500 per year or eligible tuition/mandatory fees, whichever less; maximum determined annually and funding contingent on state appropriations. Institution receives payment for degree-pursuant undergraduate coursework. Up to eight bachelor semesters or four associate semesters; normally must use within six years after award, with military extension. Completion of degree ends eligibility. Renewal normally 2.75 overall college GPA and 30 earned credits per two-semester academic year (15 for one semester), continuous full-time enrolment, with final-year exceptions.

deadline: Class of 2027: Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA open October 1, 2026; both must meet submission/processing conditions by March 1, 2027. Last qualifying SAT administration is June 2027; last qualifying national ACT is July 2027. No time zone stated.

application: Create WVSAM account, verify email, submit Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA by March 1, 2027, even if qualifying grades/scores are still pending. Send individual official test administrations (ACT code 4539, SAT 3456) and monitor matching/status. Public-school academic records generally supplied through school system; private-school final records and special homeschool/commuter/military forms require school/applicant verification. Scholars do not reapply annually; annual FAFSA encouraged for other aid.

eligibility: Class of 2027: overall high-school GPA at least 3.0/B under approved school policy; separate core GPA requirement removed. ACT composite 21 on English/reading/math or SAT 1080; superscores accepted beginning 2027-28, without mixing ACT/SAT formats. U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen. Student AND FAFSA parent/legal guardian normally need 12 consecutive months WV residency before deadline; at least half high-school credits completed at qualifying WV school and eligible graduation route. Qualified homeschool/Hope-IIP, daily out-of-state commuter, military and approved alternative-education routes require additional documents. First-time full-time initial award normally within two years of graduation, with specified exceptions.

supports: identity: New Mexico Higher Education Department confirms New Mexico Legislative Lottery Scholarship.

value: 100% of tuition at New Mexico public colleges and universities, up to seven semesters (three at community colleges). The Opportunity Scholarship can cover the first qualifying semester and course fees.

application: No separate scholarship application or FAFSA required. Enrol/register at eligible New Mexico public institution and notify financial-aid adviser that first full-time semester establishes Lottery eligibility. College determines qualification and credits award. Disability accommodation requires student-services documentation and timely notice before term.

eligibility: New Mexico resident (normally 12 consecutive months) with qualifying New Mexico high-school graduation, HSE while resident or registered homeschool completion; first bachelor not yet earned. Eligible out-of-state members of a Nation/Tribe/Pueblo wholly or partly in New Mexico can qualify with membership proof. Noncitizens may qualify through nondiscrimination waiver after at least one year New Mexico high-school attendance and qualifying NM graduation/HSE. Establish and maintain 2.50 college GPA, full-time 15 credits four-year or 12 community college within 16 months and continuous fall/spring enrolment, with disability/approved interruption exceptions.

deadline: No separate scholarship application. supports: identity: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction and North Dakota University System confirms North Dakota Scholarship.
value: $750 per semester, up to $6,000, usable at approved North Dakota colleges, universities, professional schools and registered apprenticeship programs within six years of graduation.

application: Create/use North Dakota Login and complete Class of 2027 application. School submits Choice Ready eligibility report; nonpublic schools use verification form. Homeschool applicants supply notices of intent for home-education years, notarised grades 9-12 transcript and verification, official test and dual-enrolment records. Tests must be taken before graduation; send later-than-March ACT results to NDDPI code 2927. No annual reapplication after award; institution certifies renewal.

eligibility: North Dakota resident at graduation with ND high-school diploma, including documented homeschool route. Essential Skills: 3.00 overall unweighted GPA, civics test 70%+, nine weeks career education/counselling, four-year rolling plan and four of eight additional indicators. Also complete two of three pathways: Post-Secondary Ready (ACT 24/SAT 1180 plus two approved academic indicators), Workforce Ready (required CTE/language coursework, ACT 24/SAT 1180 or WorkKeys all three scores 5+, plus two workforce indicators), Military Ready (ASVAB 50+, or 31+ with basic training within 90 days after graduation, required PE plus two indicators). ACT superscores allowed. Same dual course cannot satisfy both pathway indicators.
